o: Revise estimate of instruments expected to vest at each reporting date, trueing up cumulative expense
Retain original grant-date forfeiture estimates without subsequent adjustment
Reverse all previously recognized expenses directly to opening retained earnings
Recognize forfeiture differences in other comprehensive income as equity adjustments

q: In forensic accounting, what is the purpose of analyzing the ratio of Selling, General, and Administrative (SG&A) Expenses to Revenue across a business downturn?
o: Detects operating leverage stickiness; failing to reduce SG&A rapidly compresses operating margins
Measures compliance with statutory maximum executive compensation disclosure guidelines
Calculates the proportion of non-current plant assets financed by trade payables credit
Determines the optimal debt-to-equity capital structure to minimize the cost of capital

q: What is the primary forensic accounting risk associated with software companies that heavily capitalize internal software development costs under IAS 38?
o: Artificially depresses operating expenses, boosts reported EBITDA, and overstates balance sheet assets
Understates reported gross profit margins by accelerating software license amortization
Increases reported financial gearing and reduces return on capital employed
Forces immediate recognition of deferred tax liabilities under statutory rules

q: Under IFRS 10, what is the accounting treatment when a parent entity acquires an additional 20% stake in a subsidiary where parent already owns 60%?
o: Accounted for as an equity transaction; no gain, loss, or additional goodwill is recognized
Goodwill is recalculated under IFRS 3 and any difference recognized in profit or loss
The 20% stake is recognized as an investment in associate using the equity method
Subsidiary assets and liabilities are remeasured to fair value on the acquisition date

q: Under IFRS 3, how should an acquirer measure reacquired rights (e.g. rights previously granted to acquiree to use acquirer trade name)?
o: Recognized as an intangible asset based on remaining contractual term, ignoring renewals
Subsumed into purchased corporate goodwill on acquisition as an unidentifiable right
Expensed immediately on acquisition date as a settlement of a pre-existing contract
Measured at fair value assuming perpetual indefinite renewal by market participants

q: Under IFRS 9, what is the accounting treatment for an equity investment that does NOT meet the definition of held for trading and is NOT designated at FVOCI?
o: Mandatorily classified and measured at Fair Value Through Profit or Loss (FVTPL)
Measured at Amortized Cost using the effective interest method over ten years
Measured at lower of historical cost and net realizable value on balance sheet
Accounted for using the equity method under the provisions of IAS 28

q: Under IFRS 15, when an entity provides an extended warranty that can be purchased separately, how is the warranty accounted for?
o: As a separate performance obligation with revenue recognized over the extended warranty coverage period
As an accrued operating expense provision under IAS 37 recognized at delivery date
As a deduction from gross transaction price on the initial sales invoice date
As a contingent liability disclosed solely in financial statement footnotes

q: Under IFRS 16, what is the required accounting treatment when a lessee enters into a lease with a zero or peppercorn lease payment from government?
o: Recognize right-of-use asset and lease liability at nominal cost, or optionally at fair value under IAS 20
Mandatorily recognize ROU asset at open market replacement value with credit to operating profit
Classify as an off-balance sheet operating service agreement with zero financial disclosure
Expense estimated commercial market rent annually in operating profit or loss

q: Under IAS 19, how are administration costs of managing defined benefit pension plan assets treated?
o: Deducted from the return on plan assets in determining net interest and remeasurements
Expensed in profit or loss as general corporate administrative operating overheads
Capitalized into the carrying value of corporate goodwill on consolidated balance sheet
Deducted directly from opening consolidated retained earnings as an extraordinary charge

q: Under IAS 12, what is the deferred tax treatment for an entity operating in a jurisdiction where corporate income tax is payable only when profits are distributed as dividends?
o: Income tax consequences of dividends recognized when liability to pay dividend is recognized
Deferred tax liability recognized immediately on all undistributed accounting profits
No income tax recognized until tax authorities issue an annual statutory assessment
Income tax expense recognized in other comprehensive income as an equity tax reserve

q: Under IAS 33, what is the effect of an equity rights issue with a bonus element on Basic EPS?
o: Multiply prior period weighted shares by theoretical ex-rights price factor to restate comparatives
Weight new rights shares from the date cash consideration is received with zero comparative change
Exclude rights shares from basic EPS and include them strictly in diluted EPS calculations
Deduct nominal value of rights shares directly from operating profit before interest

q: Under IFRS 2, how is an employee share option award with a non-vesting condition (e.g. employee must contribute monthly to a savings plan) accounted for?
o: Factored into grant-date fair value; failure to meet condition is treated as a cancellation
Adjusted at each reporting date based on expected employee participation rates
Reversed in full from equity if the employee ceases monthly contributions
Treated as a cash-settled liability remeasured annually at fair value through P&L

q: In performance analysis, how is the Economic Spread calculated in value-based management?
o: Return on Invested Capital (ROIC) minus Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC)
Operating Profit Margin minus Statutory Corporate Income Tax Rate
Gross Profit Margin minus Selling, General, and Administrative Expense Ratio
Asset Turnover multiplied by Financial Leverage Equity Multiplier

q: What does a positive Economic Spread (ROIC > WACC) signify for an enterprise?
o: The entity is generating economic value and creating wealth above its cost of capital
The entity is experiencing severe operational overtrading and cash liquidity strain
The entity must immediately write down all corporate goodwill assets under IAS 36
The entity's price-to-earnings ratio automatically falls to zero on stock exchanges

q: Under IFRS 10, when an investor controls an investee through complex structured entities with zero equity ownership, what is this structured entity commonly called?
o: Special Purpose Entity (SPE) or structured entity where voting rights are not dominant
Unincorporated joint venture governed exclusively by the provisions of IFRS 11
Associate entity accounted for under the equity method of accounting in IAS 28
Non-current asset held for sale governed by the presentation rules of IFRS 5

q: Under IFRS 3, what is the accounting treatment for acquisition-related costs incurred to issue debt securities in a business combination?
o: Deducted from the initial carrying amount of the financial liability under IFRS 9
Expensed in profit or loss on the acquisition date as professional advisory fees
Capitalized as an integral element of purchase consideration in corporate goodwill
Deducted directly from parent company distributable retained earnings reserve

q: Under IFRS 9, how is a financial asset reclassified from Amortized Cost to Fair Value Through Profit or Loss (FVTPL) accounted for?
o: Fair value measured at reclassification date; difference between amortized cost and fair value recognized in P&L
Carried at previous amortized cost with adjusted effective yield rate prospectively
Difference recognized in other comprehensive income as an asset revaluation surplus
Applied retrospectively restating all prior period comparative financial figures

q: Under IFRS 15, how is a non-refundable upfront setup fee accounted for when setup activities do NOT transfer a promised good or service to customer?
o: Treated as an advance payment for future goods/services and recognized over performance period
Recognized immediately as revenue on the initial cash payment date
Expensed immediately as an operational customer onboarding cost
Recorded in other comprehensive income as a deferred service reserve

q: Under IFRS 16, what happens to the right-of-use asset and lease liability when a lessee abandons a leased property before lease term ends?
o: ROU asset is tested for impairment and written off to zero; lease liability continues to be serviced
Lease liability is derecognized immediately with full gain recognized in profit or loss
ROU asset is retained on balance sheet and depreciated straight-line over contractual term
Lease contract is reclassified as an off-balance sheet operating commitment

q: Under IAS 19, what is the accounting treatment for risk-sharing or conditional indexation features in defined benefit pension plans?
o: Reflected in the measurement of the defined benefit obligation and service cost
Ignored until indexation increases are formally declared by pension plan trustees
Recognized in other comprehensive income as an unquantified actuarial reserve
Accrued as a separate contingent liability footnote disclosure under IAS 37

q: Under IAS 12, when an entity operates across multiple tax jurisdictions, at what tax rates are deferred tax balances measured?
o: Tax rates enacted or substantively enacted at reporting date expected to apply when asset realized/liability settled
Standard domestic tax rate of the ultimate parent company holding jurisdiction
Average statutory tax rate across all international operating subsidiaries
Historical statutory corporate income tax rate on the original transaction date

q: Under IAS 33, how are share options issued by a subsidiary that are exercisable into subsidiary ordinary shares treated in consolidated Diluted EPS?
o: Included in subsidiary diluted EPS, which is then used to determine parent consolidated diluted EPS
Excluded from consolidated diluted EPS because options are issued by subsidiary, not parent
Subtracted directly from parent company operating profit attributable to equity holders
Reclassified as long-term financial liabilities on the consolidated balance sheet

q: Under IFRS 2, when an employer provides loans to employees to purchase shares that are non-recourse (secured only by shares), how is the arrangement treated?
o: Accounted for as a grant of share options (substance of non-recourse loan is an option)
Accounted for as a financial asset loan receivable measured at amortized cost under IFRS 9
Recognized as an immediate cash bonus expense in operating profit or loss
Treated as an equity rights issue with zero share-based payment accounting

q: In financial analysis, what does the Modified DuPont Formula (ROE = Operating Margin x Asset Turnover x Leverage Multiplier x Interest Burden x Tax Burden) isolate?
o: Separates operational performance, financing efficiency, and tax management drivers of equity return
Calculates the precise statistical probability of imminent corporate bankruptcy within twelve months
Measures compliance with mandatory international financial reporting disclosure standards
Determines the optimal working capital cash conversion cycle duration in days

q: What is the primary indicator of earnings manipulation through aggressive channel inventory build in wholesale distribution?
o: Receivables and revenues expand rapidly while distributor sales to end-users remain stagnant
Inventory holding period declines sharply across consecutive financial quarters
Operating cash flow increases significantly relative to reported operating profit
Gross profit margins decline due to higher prompt payment trade discounts

q: Under IFRS 10, when an investment entity ceases to meet the definition of an investment entity, how is the change accounted for?
o: Applied prospectively: former fair value of subsidiaries is deemed consideration in IFRS 3 consolidation
Applied retrospectively restating all prior period comparative financial figures
Recognized as an extraordinary adjustment in opening group retained earnings
Subsidiaries are accounted for as associates using the equity method under IAS 28

q: Under IFRS 3, what is the accounting treatment for an acquirer's transaction costs incurred to issue equity shares as consideration in a business combination?
o: Deducted directly from share premium account (or equity) under IAS 32 rules
Expensed in profit or loss on the acquisition date as professional advisory fees
Capitalized as an integral element of purchase consideration in corporate goodwill
Recognized in other comprehensive income as an equity issuance reserve

q: Under IFRS 9, how is a financial asset reclassified from Fair Value Through Profit or Loss (FVTPL) to Amortized Cost accounted for?
o: Fair value at reclassification date becomes new gross carrying amount; effective rate determined
Carried forward at original historical cost with retrospective prior year restatement
Difference recognized in other comprehensive income as an asset revaluation surplus
Applied retrospectively restating opening group retained earnings balances

q: Under IFRS 15, how is a customer contract involving customer-furnished materials (e.g. customer supplies fabric for garment production) treated?
o: Entity assesses whether it obtains control of materials; if not, materials excluded from revenue and cost
Entity must recognize gross fair value of materials as revenue and cost of goods sold
Materials recognized as inventory asset with corresponding credit to customer advance liabilities
Treated as a non-monetary barter exchange under the measurement rules of IAS 16

q: Under IFRS 16, what is the required presentation for lessor cash flows received from operating leases in the statement of cash flows?
o: Classified as operating cash inflows in the statement of cash flows
Classified as investing cash inflows alongside non-current asset sales
Classified as financing cash inflows alongside debt borrowings
Deducted directly from lease receivables on the balance sheet

q: Under IAS 19, what happens to actuarial assumptions regarding mortality rates when updating the defined benefit obligation?
o: Updated mortality assumptions produce actuarial gains/losses recognized in OCI
Expensed in profit or loss as an exceptional employee compensation cost
Recognized in other comprehensive income and recycled to profit over 5 years
Deferred on balance sheet and amortized against future employer contributions

q: Under IAS 12, what is the deferred tax treatment for a deductible temporary difference when future taxable profits are insufficient to utilize the full deduction?
o: Deferred tax asset recognized only to the extent of available future taxable profit
Deferred tax asset recognized in full with a valuation allowance disclosed in notes
Deferred tax asset written off completely with zero balance sheet recognition
Charged directly to opening group retained earnings as a prior period error

q: Under IAS 33, what is the required disclosure when an entity has ordinary transactions after the reporting date that would have changed the number of shares significantly?
o: Disclose description of transactions in notes, without adjusting Basic or Diluted EPS
Retrospectively adjust Basic and Diluted EPS for the reporting period ended
Restate opening retained earnings to reflect post-balance sheet equity changes
Withhold publication of financial statements until share issue completes

q: Under IFRS 2, if an entity grants share options with a reload feature, how is the reload feature accounted for?
o: Accounted for as a new option grant when the reload option is subsequently granted
Factored into the initial grant-date fair value of the original option award
Treated as a modification of the original option award increasing fair value
Recognized as a cash-settled liability remeasured annually at fair value through P&L

q: In financial performance analysis, what does the Tobin's Q ratio (Market Value of Assets / Replacement Cost of Assets) indicate when Q > 1?
o: The firm has valuable unrecorded intangible assets, brand equity, or growth opportunities
The firm is overvalued and faces imminent operational insolvency in the near term
The firm has zero long-term debt gearing on its published statement of financial position
The firm's historical return on capital employed is strictly below the industry average

q: What is the primary forensic accounting technique for identifying unrecorded liabilities at year-end?
o: Search for unrecorded liabilities: examining cash disbursements after year-end against unpaid invoices
Recalculating historical asset depreciation schedules using alternative straight-line rates
Confirming trade customer receivable balances through formal positive circularization letters
Revaluing investment property at fair value certified by independent commercial surveyors

q: Under IFRS 10, how is a deemed disposal accounted for when a subsidiary issues share options to third parties that dilute the parent's ownership without losing control?
o: Accounted for as an equity transaction; difference recognized directly in consolidated equity
Recognized in consolidated statement of profit or loss as an operational disposal gain
Purchased corporate goodwill is recalculated under the provisions of IFRS 3
The investment is derecognized and accounted for as an associate under IAS 28

q: Under IFRS 3, how should an acquirer account for contingent liabilities of an acquiree if the contingency is subsequently settled during the measurement period?
o: Measurement period adjustment to goodwill only if it reflects facts existing at acquisition date
Recognized in profit or loss in the period of settlement under all operational circumstances
Adjusted against parent company share premium account within consolidated shareholders' equity
Deferred on the statement of financial position and amortized over twenty operating years

q: Under IFRS 9, what is the accounting treatment for a synthetic lease where an entity leases an asset designed solely to keep debt off the balance sheet?
o: IFRS 16 eliminates synthetic leases by requiring ROU asset and lease liability recognition on balance sheet
Synthetic leases remain off-balance sheet operating commitments with supplementary footnote disclosure
Accounted for as a derivative financial instrument measured at fair value through profit or loss
Recognized as an intangible asset amortized straight-line over fifty commercial years

q: Under IFRS 15, when is revenue from custom manufacturing recognized over time under the alternative use and enforceable right to payment criterion?
o: Asset has no alternative use to entity and entity has enforceable right to payment for performance to date
Customer pays fifty percent cash deposit upfront and factory signs storage insurance policy
The customized product can be easily resold to alternative customers at nominal discount
The manufacturing process is certified by international quality standards organizations

q: Under IFRS 16, how is a lease of land and building accounted for by a lessor?
o: Land and building elements assessed separately as finance or operating leases unless land is immaterial
Combined and classified as a single operating lease under all commercial circumstances
Classified automatically as a finance lease because real estate maintains residual value
Derecognized immediately with gross selling profit recognized in statement of profit or loss

q: Under IAS 19, what happens to defined benefit plan assets when a plan is overfunded and the employer decides to terminate the plan and distribute surplus to employees?
o: Recognized as a settlement: gain or loss recognized in profit or loss on the settlement date
Transferred directly to other comprehensive income as an employee benefit reserve
Deducted directly from opening consolidated retained earnings as an extraordinary adjustment
Deferred on the statement of financial position and amortized over ten future years

q: Under IAS 12, what is the deferred tax treatment for an entity that has taxable temporary differences related to revalued buildings that will be recovered through continuing use rather than sale?
o: Deferred tax liability measured at tax rate applicable to operating trading profits, not capital gains rate
Deferred tax liability measured at statutory capital gains tax rate applicable to asset disposal
No deferred tax liability recognized because building is recovered through depreciation
Deferred tax asset recognized reflecting future accounting depreciation deductions

q: Under IAS 33, what is the required presentation when an entity presents both consolidated and separate financial statements?
o: EPS disclosures required only in consolidated statements; if presented in separate, only on face of separate P&L
EPS disclosures required exclusively in parent separate financial statements, omitted from group
EPS disclosures required in both statements with identical numerical per-share figures
EPS disclosures prohibited in separate financial statements under statutory regulations

q: Under IFRS 2, how is an employee share-based payment award with a performance target based on a non-market operational metric (e.g. EBITDA growth) accounted for if the target is not achieved?
o: No expense is ultimately recognized in financial statements; cumulative expense is trued up to zero
Previously recognized expense remains permanently recognized in equity without reversal
Expense is transferred from equity to a current cash compensation refund liability
Award is remeasured to fair value with an exceptional gain recognized in operating profit

q: In financial statement analysis, what does the Cash Flow Quality Ratio (Cash Flow from Operations / Net Income) consistently below 0.8 indicate?
o: Poor earnings quality: reported profits are heavily reliant on accounting accruals rather than cash collections
Superior operational efficiency: company generates strong recurring core trading profitability
Prudent conservatism: management suppresses operating profit to minimize corporate taxes
Impaired liquidity: enterprise is unable to collect cash from primary trade customers

q: What is the primary indicator of balance sheet cookie-jar reserve manipulation in corporate financial reporting?
o: Unjustified releases of previously overstated restructuring or legal provisions to bolster earnings in weak years
Consistent capitalization of routine manufacturing maintenance expenditures into non-current plant
Accelerated depreciation of fully functioning plant assets to minimize current statutory taxes
Reclassification of short-term bank debt facilities into long-term subordinated debentures

q: Under IAS 10, if an entity announces a major restructuring after the reporting date, how must it be treated?
o: Disclosed as a non-adjusting event if material, explaining nature and financial estimate
Recognized as an adjusting event with full restructuring provision on balance sheet
Accounted for as a prior period fundamental error restating opening retained earnings
Ignored completely because board announcements do not constitute legal contracts

q: Under IAS 1, what is the required presentation when an entity reclassifies items in its financial statements?
o: Reclassify comparative amounts and present three statements of financial position
Present comparative amounts unchanged and disclose changes only in directors' report
Obtain express written permission from national capital market regulatory agencies
Restate opening share capital and share premium accounts by the reclassified amounts

q: Under IFRS 13, when is a valuation adjustment (such as a Credit Valuation Adjustment - CVA or Debit Valuation Adjustment - DVA) incorporated?
o: In measuring the fair value of derivative instruments to reflect counterparty and own credit risk
Only when calculating the carrying value of trade receivables under the simplified model
In adjusting the initial fair value of corporate goodwill recognized on business combination
Exclusively for financial assets measured at amortized cost using effective interest rates

q: Under IAS 36, how should an impairment loss allocated to an individual asset be recognized if the asset cannot be written down below its recoverable amount?
o: Remaining impairment is allocated pro-rata to other assets of the cash-generating unit
Remaining impairment is written off against parent company distributable retained earnings
Remaining impairment is capitalized as an addition to group corporate goodwill
Remaining impairment is deferred on the balance sheet until the asset is disposed of

q: Under IAS 38, how are subsequent expenditures on an acquired brand or customer list accounted for?
o: Expensed in profit or loss when incurred, because they maintain rather than enhance brand
Capitalized into the carrying amount of the brand if approved by marketing directors
Added to the carrying value of purchased corporate goodwill on consolidated balance sheet
Recorded in other comprehensive income as an intangible asset revaluation surplus

q: Under IFRS 15, what is the accounting treatment for customer returns under a right-of-return sales contract?
o: Recognize revenue for expected kept goods, refund liability for returns, and return asset
Recognize gross revenue upon dispatch and record an estimated warranty provision under IAS 37
Defer entire contract revenue until customer statutory return right period expires
Expense estimated return costs immediately as administrative overhead allowances

q: Under IFRS 16, what criteria determine whether a contract contains an identified asset?
o: Explicitly or implicitly specified, and supplier does NOT have substantive substitution rights
Asset is legally registered with statutory national transport or property registries
Customer holds legal freehold ownership title to the physical asset throughout contract term
The contract contains an unconditional guarantee of replacement within twenty-four hours

q: Under IFRS 9, when an entity reclassifies a financial asset out of FVOCI into Amortized Cost, how is the accumulated gain or loss in OCI treated?
o: Removed from OCI and adjusted against fair value of asset at reclassification date
Recycled immediately to profit or loss on the formal reclassification date
Retained permanently in other comprehensive income without adjustment
Transferred directly to statutory capital redemption reserve within equity

q: Under IAS 19, how is a reimbursement right (e.g. insurance policy to cover pension obligations) accounted for?
o: Recognized as a separate asset at fair value, not offset against defined benefit liability
Offset directly against the present value of the defined benefit obligation on balance sheet
Treated as plan assets and included in the net defined benefit deficit calculation
Disclosed solely as an unquantified contingent asset footnote disclosure

q: Under IAS 12, what deferred tax treatment applies to share issue costs that are deducted directly from equity but deductible for tax purposes?
o: Deferred tax benefit recognized directly in equity matching the underlying share issue cost
Deferred tax benefit recognized in profit or loss as an operating corporation tax credit
Deferred tax benefit recognized in other comprehensive income as a capital tax reserve
No deferred tax recognized because transactions in equity are exempt from taxation

q: Under IAS 33, what is the required treatment for preference shares that are cumulative when calculating Basic EPS in a year when the company reports a net loss?
o: Deduct the preference dividend, increasing the basic loss per share attributable to owners
Omit the preference dividend because dividends cannot be paid out of accounting losses
Add the preference dividend back to the net loss to reduce the reported loss per share
Reclassify preference shares as long-term financial debt liabilities on the balance sheet

q: Under IFRS 2, what is the accounting treatment when an employer settles an employee share option award by delivering shares held in treasury?
o: Accounted for as an equity-settled share award; reissuance of treasury shares is recorded in equity
Accounted for as a cash-settled liability remeasured at fair value through profit or loss
Gain or loss recognized in profit or loss based on historical treasury share purchase price
Treated as a dividend distribution reducing distributable parent company retained earnings

q: In financial performance analysis, what does a persistent increase in Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) combined with an expanding allowance for expected credit losses indicate?
o: Deteriorating customer credit quality, potential uncollectible sales, and delayed collections
Significant operational improvements in working capital cash conversion efficiency
Conservative revenue recognition policies designed to defer corporate income taxes
Rapid expansion of export sales to high-growth sovereign foreign governments

q: Under IFRS 10, what constitutes de facto agency where an entity acts as an agent for another investor without formal contractual agency status?
o: When other parties act on behalf of investor due to economic dependence or related party ties
When the investor holds exactly fifty percent of issued voting ordinary share capital
When the investee is located in an overseas jurisdiction with different legal systems
When external statutory auditors identify significant internal control deficiencies

q: Under IFRS 3, how should an acquirer account for contingent payments that become payable to former owners only if certain post-combination sales targets are met and employment is retained?
o: Classified as post-combination employee remuneration expensed in P&L over the retention period
Classified as contingent purchase consideration capitalized into initial corporate goodwill
Recognized as a separate equity reserve within consolidated shareholders' equity
Treated as an adjustment to the fair value of net identifiable assets acquired

q: Under IFRS 9, what is the required accounting treatment for financial assets purchased at a deep discount that reflect incurred credit losses?
o: Classified as POCI and measured using a credit-adjusted effective interest rate
Measured at nominal par value with an immediate 12-month expected credit loss provision
Recognized at historical purchase cost and amortized straight-line over five years
Classified as fair value through other comprehensive income with mandatory recycling

q: Under IFRS 15, how is a customer option to acquire additional goods or services at a significant discount accounted for?
o: Accounted for as a separate performance obligation, allocating part of the transaction price
Expensed as a marketing and sales promotion cost when the option is exercised
Recognized as revenue immediately on the date the initial sales contract is executed
Deducted from sales revenue as an estimated customer bad debt provision allowance

q: Under IFRS 16, what is the accounting treatment when a lessee enters into a lease modification that increases the scope of the lease by adding the right to use one or more underlying assets at standalone price?
o: Accounted for as a separate new lease, leaving the existing lease accounting unchanged
Treated as a remeasurement of the existing lease liability using a revised discount rate
Derecognizes the existing lease in full and recognizes a single combined replacement lease
Expenses all additional lease payments in operating profit or loss as incurred costs
